episodes.180192: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a severe wind gust and a funnel cloud near Cape Canaveral.
episodes.180193: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.180287: Evening sea breeze convection produced severe wind gust near Suncoast Estates in Lee County.
episodes.180431: Upper-level troughing and a weak surface trough to the lee of the Appalachians allowed for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 27, 2023. A few of these storms were able to produce sporadic wind damage across the Lower Susquehanna Valley.
episodes.180581: Some afternoon thunderstorms managed to produce a couple of funnel clouds over parts of northeastern Montana.
episodes.180810: Strong upper level system approaching from the west led to severe thunderstorm development along and east of the Laramie range on the 28th with one particular storm tracking across northeast Laramie County producing large hail up to 4 inches in diameter. This storm continued into the southern Nebraska Panhandle where it eventually produced a tornado.
episodes.180811: Strong upper level system led to severe thunderstorm development moving into the western Nebraska Panhandle on the 28th with one particular storm tracking across Kimball County producing an EF0 tornado.
episodes.181212: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm developed over the northern Black Hills and tracked eastward across west central South Dakota, producing large hail and wind gusts over 70 mph. Considerable damage to property was reported north of Rapid City as the storm passed through the area.
episodes.181216: A severe thunderstorm developed southeast of Rapid City and tracked east across portions of west central South Dakota. The storm produced large hail and eventually strong wind gusts as it tracked into south central South Dakota and merged into a line with other storms.
episodes.181219: A thunderstorm briefly became severe as it tracked from central into eastern portions of Pennington County. The storm produced hail to quarter size from New Underwood to near Wasta.
episodes.181222: Strong to severe thunderstorms merged into a line as they moved into and across south central South Dakota. Large hail and wind gusts over 75 mph were reported across parts of the area.
episodes.181247: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northern portions of Weston County, producing quarter sized hail north of Osage.
episodes.181248: A severe thunderstorm developed just east of Rapid City, producing quarter sized hail.
episodes.181249: A severe thunderstorm developed on the north side of the Rapid City area, producing hail near golf ball size from north Rapid City to Box Elder.
episodes.181251: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the northeastern foothills of the Black Hills and adjacent plains, producing hail to quarter size in the Tilford area.
episodes.181255: A severe thunderstorm developed over Rapid City, mostly affecting central and southern parts of the city. The storm produced hail to golf ball size in some areas.
episodes.181256: A strong thunderstorm produced penny sized hail in the Summerset area.
episodes.181257: A severe thunderstorm developed over northeastern Custer County, weakening as it moved into southeastern Pennington County. The storm produced hail to golf ball size in the Folsom area.
episodes.181313: A surface front was shifting south across Georgia with a surge in moist WSW flow off of the Gulf of Mexico under a passing short wave trough and bulk shear of 20-25 kts. Intrusion of drier air from the NW exacerbated DCAPE values well over 1000 J/kg and supported strong downburst winds in scattered severe storms that developed across NE FL in the evening.
episodes.181333: A generally weak/sub-severe cluster of thunderstorms/small mesoscale convective system (MCS) approached the forecast area towards daybreak on the 27th. While the background severe weather environment was modest, strengthening of the system occurred across east-central Oklahoma, with significant severe wind events noted across Payne County. Into the evening of the 27th, a mature MCS developed across far southwestern Kansas/Oklahoma Panhandle and subsequently moved across portions of northern Oklahoma. A few severe caliber wind gusts were measured across the area through the late evening hours.
episodes.181350: A surface front was shifting south across Georgia with a surge in moist WSW flow off of the Gulf of Mexico under a passing short wave trough and bulk shear of 20-25 kts. Intrusion of drier air from the NW exacerbated DCAPE values well over 1000 J/kg and supported strong downburst winds in scattered severe storms that developed across NE FL in the evening.
episodes.181377: Active weather due to an approaching tropical wave and an upper level trough was observed along the local waters by the end of the month. One of these storms was able to generate a waterspout north of Carolina.
episodes.181636: In the late afternoon of the 27th, a few storm cells began to pop up in eastern Colorado. The cell in Kit Carson county rapidly grew and then collapsed and created a 60 mph wind gust. Another cell in northern Yuma county produced hail up to 1.75 inches just before moving into Nebraska.
episodes.182063: Thunderstorms developed over the area, with one storm producing penny size hail in Foster County.
episodes.182066: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a surface trough that dropped through the area from a low over Manitoba. Initially, multiple funnel clouds were observed in the Rolla area of Rolette County, where at one point three funnels were observed simultaneously. Later, penny sized hail occurred near Rolette, along with a 58 mph wind gust.  During the evening hours, nickel sized hail fell in Foster County.
episodes.182077: Two rounds of rain moved across the state on June 28th with a weak frontal boundary. Light rain showers pushed through the state during the morning, with the first line of showers and thunderstorms moving into western New Hampshire by midday. This line slowly moved eastward through the early afternoon hours bringing a widespread band of heavy rain of 1 to 2���.  As the axis of heavy rain moved into the Lakes Region of New Hampshire, additional storms developed ahead of it.  Heavier rainfall amounts fell from Tilton through the Lake Winnipesaukee region into Moultonborough where 2 to 3��� of rain fell in less than 2 hours. This band of heavy rain continued to push further north and east by late afternoon into the White Mountains. The localized heaviest rain fell in Jackson and Bartlett New Hampshire where 3 inches of rain fell in 2 hours.  An additional line of showers and thunderstorms later in the day dropped additional localized heavy rainfall on areas that just received soaking rain a few hours earlier. One storm dropped an additional 1.5��� of rain in less than an hour north of Lebanon, NH.
episodes.182086: Very high winds from thunderstorms on 06/27.
episodes.182429: Storms dropped quarter sized hail in Northeastern North Dakota in the afternoon and evening of June 27th.
episodes.182493: Southwest flow aloft, combined with a surface trough, brought several rounds of severe thunderstorms to the area. Hail up to 4 inches in diameter and wind gusts to 63 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.182569: Thunderstorms developed in the lee of the Bighorn Range and became severe as they moved into more humid air. Ping Pong ball size hail was reported from one thunderstorm as it passed north of Kaycee. The public reported a funnel cloud to the east of Buffalo a couple of hours later from a different thunderstorm.
episodes.182575: On the evening of the 27th, a convective complex developed in the northwestern combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. This system moved northeast into Texas County in Oklahoma Panhandle where it continued to strengthen and take a more easterly direction into Beaver County. Good dynamics and an unstable airmass lead to cells with in this complex that managed to drop hail between 1 and 4 in diameter and even produced some strong winds. Of which a 114 mph wind gust that was measured by the Beaver mesonet.
episodes.182611: Thunderstorms developed and moved northeast across southeast portions of Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties. One storm produced a severe wind gust near Bowie.
episodes.182612: A line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front draped across Oklahoma and Arkansas. These storms organized into a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) over eastern Oklahoma and begin racing southeastward. Some of these storms were strong enough to produce severe winds as they reached southwest Mississippi.
episodes.182733: Thunderstorms impacted the region bringing damage and flash flooding to Eastern Washington.
episodes.182818: Severe thunderstorms moved in from western Kansas and brought strong wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph to south central Kansas. No damage was reported.
episodes.182833: Additional strong thunderstorms and weak tornadoes finished off June due to anomalous moisture in southern Colorado.
episodes.182893: A typically warm and moist airmass across Florida led to the development of a few strong thunderstorms over Lake Okeechobee and the Atlantic waters during the afternoon.
episodes.182922: Thunderstorms moved over the coastal waters, sounds, and inland rivers of Eastern NC in the afternoon into the evening producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.183724: A line of strong storms produced damaging winds across western Mississippi.
